page: Amazon Web Services m6i.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz and includes 54 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average performance in single-core operations, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1885.19 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1434.0. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3857.84 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3127.0. Memory bandwidth is also positioned in the lower tier, with read-only large block bandwidth at 29.35 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 24.45 GB/sec. Multi-threaded decompression is a notable bottleneck, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the bottom 10% at 19.04 GB/sec.

Given its balanced resource allocation, the m6i.xlarge offers a standard entry-level general-purpose profile. It is best suited for workloads that do not demand high multi-threaded throughput or intensive memory bandwidth, such as static web serving, where it achieves an average throughput of 6.51 GB/sec, or basic single-threaded text and data processing. It represents a standard cost-to-resource tier for general-purpose Intel-based compute, though workloads requiring high-performance database operations or intensive software compilation may encounter performance limitations due to the weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth characteristics.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, running on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1434.0 and static web serving throughput of 6.51 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3857.84 and large-block read bandwidth of 29.35 GB/sec. This instance is best utilized for light web serving, single-threaded processing, and basic administrative workloads that do not require high parallel processing power or intensive memory throughput.
